title: Affine generic-field data for finite covers of normal integral schemes
statement: Let $p:Y\to Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme], and suppose that every local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $\eta_Y,\eta_Z$ for their generic points [def-sc-generic-point], $K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ and $L=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta_Z}$ for their function fields [def-sc-function-field, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $p(\eta_Y)=\eta_Z$, and the map on generic stalks is a field embedding $\iota:L\hookrightarrow K$ making $K$ finite-dimensional over $L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Put $d=\dim_LK\geq1$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], its inverse image is a nonempty affine open $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$, and $p^\sharp:B\to A$ is an injective homomorphism of domains making $A$ a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The ring $B$ is integrally closed in its fraction field. The generic-germ embeddings $\rho_U:B\hookrightarrow L$ and $\sigma_U:A\hookrightarrow K$ identify $L$ and $K$ as fields of fractions of $B$ and $A$, respectively; that is, their elements are quotients of images of ring elements with nonzero denominator. They satisfy $\sigma_U(p^\sharp b)=\iota(\rho_U(b))$ for every $b\in B$. For nested nonempty affine opens $W\subseteq U$, taking a generic germ commutes with restriction for both $\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal O_Y$. Thus all these affine fraction-field extensions have the single degree $d$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), first paragraph: affine domains and the common fraction-field extension; the normal-base hypothesis needed for descent of minimal polynomials. Expanded affine normality and generic-field identifications from returned proof steps 1 and 2.

proof.text: First $p(\eta_Y)=\eta_Z$. Indeed, let $V\subseteq Z$ be nonempty open. Surjectivity makes $p^{-1}V$ nonempty, and continuity makes it open. A nonempty open of $Y$ contains $\eta_Y$: otherwise the closed complement would contain $\eta_Y$ and hence its closure $Y$. Thus $p(\eta_Y)\in V$. Consequently the closure of $\{p(\eta_Y)\}$ is $Z$, since its complement, if nonempty, would be a nonempty open missing this point. The uniqueness of the generic point of an irreducible scheme, supplied by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], identifies it with $\eta_Z$.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), affine-field setup; generic-point argument expanded using Tag 01IS (schemes-lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Z$. By the definition of finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $p^{-1}U$ is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $A$ is a finite $B$-module. This inverse image is nonempty by surjectivity. Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to $Z,U$ and to $Y,p^{-1}U$: $B,A$ are domains; $L,K$ are fields; the generic-germ maps $\rho_U:B\to L$ and $\sigma_U:A\to K$ are injective and exhibit the respective target fields as their fraction fields. This application is to opens of the original integral schemes, so it needs no normality of $Y$ or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), first paragraph; fraction fields: Morphisms Tag 01RV (morphisms-lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions).

proof.text: The morphism of locally ringed spaces underlying $p$ induces a unital ring map on stalks at $\eta_Y$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Step 1 identifies its source with $L$, so call this map $\iota:L\to K$. It is injective: if $0\ne c\in L$ mapped to zero, then $1=\iota(cc^{-1})=0$, contradicting that $K$ is a field. By the definition of the induced stalk map on a representative section and of germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], for every $b\in B$ one has $\iota(\rho_U(b))=(p^\sharp b)_{\eta_Y}=\sigma_U(p^\sharp b)$. If $p^\sharp b=0$, this identity and the two injections $\iota,\rho_U$ give $b=0$. Thus $p^\sharp:B\to A$ is an injective map of domains.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), displayed square; definitions of morphism and stalk maps: Schemes Tag 01HA (schemes-section-locally-ringed-spaces) and Sheaves Tag 0078 (section-stalks).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree], the finite injective domain algebra $B\hookrightarrow A$ of steps 2--3 induces a finite-dimensional extension of fraction fields. Use exactly the fraction-field identifications given by $\rho_U,\sigma_U$ in step 2. The induced map on a quotient is $\rho_U(b)/\rho_U(c)\mapsto\sigma_U(p^\sharp b)/\sigma_U(p^\sharp c)$ for $c\ne0$. Step 3 identifies this with $\iota(\rho_U(b)/\rho_U(c))$. Every element of $L$ is such a quotient, so the induced extension is precisely $\iota:L\hookrightarrow K$, and $d=\dim_LK$ is finite. A basis of the nonzero vector space $K$ cannot be empty (the span of the empty family is $0$, whereas $1\ne0$), so $d\geq1$. A nonempty affine $U$ exists because schemes are locally affine and $Z$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0BD3 (divisors-lemma-norm-in-normal-case), sentence "Since K/L is a finite extension"; finite-domain fraction-degree algebraic input.

proof.text: To verify normality of $B$, let $t\in L$ be a root of a monic polynomial over $B$. For every $z\in U$, [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] embeds $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ into $L$ and makes $L$ its fraction field; the embedding sends the germ of $b\in B$ to $\rho_U(b)$. Thus the same monic equation shows that $t$ is integral over $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The hypothesis that this local ring is integrally closed, with the meaning in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], implies $t\in\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ inside $L$. Applying [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] to the integral scheme $Z$, the open $U$, and this one element $t$ gives $b\in\mathcal O_Z(U)=B$ with $\rho_U(b)=t$. Therefore every element of the fraction field of $B$ integral over $B$ belongs to $B$, as required. No finiteness of the cover, local Noetherianity, or restriction on dimension was used.

source.place: Tags 033L (properties-lemma-integral-normal) and 0358 (properties-lemma-normal-integral-sections); the local-to-global step is expanded by the generic-germ gluing criterion, rather than invoking a Noetherian criterion.

proof.text: For nonempty affine opens $W\subseteq U$, the germ of $b|_W$ at $\eta_Z$ equals the germ of $b$ at $\eta_Z$: both represent the same element of the directed colimit over neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The identical argument on $Y$ applies to $p^{-1}W\subseteq p^{-1}U$. The section maps $p^\sharp$ commute with these restrictions by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so the commuting square in step 3 is compatible with both restrictions. Thus every affine fraction-field extension is the same actual map $\iota:L\hookrightarrow K$, with degree the single integer $d$ of step 4.

lean.statement: theorem finite_normal_cover_affine_field_data {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y] [IsIntegral Z] (p : Y ⟶ Z) [IsFinite p] [Surjective p] (hZ : ∀ z : Z, IsDomain (Z.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Z.presheaf.stalk z)) : ∃ hη : p (genericPoint Y) = genericPoint Z, Function.Injective (p.functionFieldMap hη).hom ∧ (p.functionFieldMap hη).hom.Finite ∧ ∃ d : ℕ, d = @Module.finrank Z.functionField Y.functionField _ _ (p.functionFieldMap hη).hom.toAlgebra.toModule ∧ 1 ≤ d ∧ ∀ (U : Z.Opens) (_hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U], ∃ _hpre : Nonempty (p ⁻¹ᵁ U), IsAffineOpen (p ⁻¹ᵁ U) ∧ IsDomain Γ(Z, U) ∧ IsDomain Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ U) ∧ Function.Injective (p.app U).hom ∧ (p.app U).hom.Finite ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed Γ(Z, U) ∧ Function.Injective (Z.germToFunctionField U).hom ∧ Function.Injective (Y.germToFunctionField (p ⁻¹ᵁ U)).hom ∧ IsFractionRing Γ(Z, U) Z.functionField ∧ IsFractionRing Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ U) Y.functionField ∧ (∀ b : Γ(Z, U), Y.germToFunctionField (p ⁻¹ᵁ U) (p.app U b) = p.functionFieldMap hη (Z.germToFunctionField U b)) ∧ (∀ (W : Z.Opens) (_hW : IsAffineOpen W) [Nonempty W] (hWU : W ≤ U) [Nonempty (p ⁻¹ᵁ W)], (∀ b : Γ(Z, U), Z.germToFunctionField W (Z.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWU).op b) = Z.germToFunctionField U b) ∧ (∀ a : Γ(Y, p ⁻¹ᵁ U), Y.germToFunctionField (p ⁻¹ᵁ W) (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (p.preimage_mono hWU)).op a) = Y.germToFunctionField (p ⁻¹ᵁ U) a))
